description.value: A backcountry campsite within Cape Scott Provincial Park, reached only by multi-kilometre hiking trail through old-growth rainforest at Vancouver Island's remote northwestern tip; loaded bikes cannot approach — this is strictly hike-in wilderness camping. No vehicle access, basic facilities, and full coastal exposure make this a committed undertaking.

raw_osm.description: Small muddy campground. Fresh water from strong creek. Two sets of partially-built pads. No set firepit. One outhouse and bear box.
raw_osm.name: Fisherman's Creek

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The primary evidence sources are the OSM tags (which include a detailed description: 'Small muddy campground. Fresh water from strong creek. Two sets of partially-built pads. No set firepit. One outhouse and bear box.' and amenity=bear_box) and the BC Parks Cape Scott Park website, which confirms this is a remote backcountry wilderness area at the northwestern tip of Vancouver Island accessible only by hiking/backpacking. The website does not mention Fisherman's Creek specifically by name, so OSM tags are the authoritative source for site-level amenities. Animal-safe food storage is confirmed by both the OSM amenity=bear_box tag and the OSM description explicitly mentioning a bear box.
concerns: The OSM website URL points to the general Cape Scott Park page; Fisherman's Creek is not mentioned by name anywhere in the fetched website content, so all site-level detail relies solely on OSM tags.
Site is tagged backcountry=yes and is described as a remote wilderness campground — no road or trail access by bicycle is evidenced.
OSM description notes the campground is 'small' and 'muddy' with only partially-built tent pads and no set firepit, suggesting very basic and potentially unfinished infrastructure.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Fisherman's Creek is a legitimate BC Parks backcountry campsite, but it is accessible only by multi-day hiking/backpacking trails within a remote wilderness park — there is no evidence it is reachable by bicycle. Its value to a cycling tourism directory depends on whether the WWC scope includes hike-in backcountry sites along the Cape Scott trail network.
enrichment_extras.notes: Fresh water is available from the creek on site per OSM description, but should be treated before drinking. The bear box is the only confirmed food-storage amenity.
